Section 2.2.1: 'The DfM-process identifies five different steps (Fig. 2.2): analysis, concept, design, construction and the experience together with the evaluation. For the analysis and conceptualisation of the framework of haptic design parameters we rely on the research conducted in the theoretical and empirical track. The design and construction of the framework and its parameters are addressed in the design track, and the assessment of the parameters and their framework takes place in the evaluation track.' (p. 57)
title: Designing Architecture for More: A Framework of Haptic Design Parameters with the Experience of People Born Blind

findings.antecedent: Home visits with adults born blind, photo-ethnographic tours by children born blind, focus group interviews with caregivers
findings.consequent: Identification of haptic qualities and obstacles regarding the built environment, insights into people's haptic perception, relevance for sensory research
findings.quote: The findings of these theoretical and empirical studies are threefold. On the one hand haptic qualities and obstacles regarding the built environment are identified. In addition, the results inform us on people’s haptic perception of the environment. Finally, the different research methods turn out to be relevant for sensory research.

findings.consequent: Interaction between context, experience and design parameters
findings.quote: haptic experience in the built environment relies on an interaction between context, experience and design parameters

findings.antecedent: Context (modes of touch, perceived affordance of planes, sensitivity of body parts)
findings.quote: Every possible combination in this main framework consists its own values for the design parameters linked to the experiential values.

findings.consequent: Material properties (texture, elasticity, air permeability, specific gravity, temperature) and geometrical properties (curvature, orientation, configuration, size)
findings.quote: The haptic design parameters are described by material properties and geometrical properties. We consider texture, elasticity, air permeability, specific gravity and temperature as material parameters. Curvature, orientation, configuration and size are geometrical parameters.

findings.consequent: Resonates with experiences of different users (visually impaired and not visually impaired)
findings.quote: The findings of the focus group interview suggest that the framework of haptic parameters resonates with the experiences of different users

findings.consequent: Challenges with a sensory paradox (questioning visual bias but used visually)
findings.quote: the framework’s representation challenges us with a sensory paradox: while the parameters question the visual bias in architectural design, they are meant to be used by designers, who are used to think, know and work in a visual way.

mechanism_chain.description: Haptic and auditory environmental cues provide sensory input, which is processed perceptually and cognitively to build a spatial mental model, leading to improved navigation, safety, and a richer experience of the built environment for people born blind.

theory_commitments.specific_claim: Cognition, including spatial understanding and navigation, is deeply dependent on the body's sensory and motor interactions with the physical environment, particularly for individuals relying on non-visual senses.

Information from different sensory modalities (e.g., haptic, auditory, proprioceptive) is combined to form a coherent and robust perception of the environment, crucial for spatial awareness in the absence of sight.

Design should be accessible and usable by all people, to the greatest extent possible, without the need for adaptation or specialized design, with this paper specifically extending these principles to haptic dimensions for people born blind.
